release.note: these are the tarballs the release tag "latest" held for bb5a8550 on 2026-11-23 (both bundles say build bb5a855); CI deletes and recreates that tag on every release build of main, so the files move or vanish. Setup takes a tarball from pkg/tarballs, then from the cache, then from the release, refuses any whose sha256 differs from the pin or whose bundle names another build, and keeps a copy of each in the cache, which survives removing <contenders>/scramjet
release.fallback: once the tag has moved and the cache is empty, put the two files in the cache by hand: from a saved copy, or built from source at bb5a8550 as CI builds them (git clone, git checkout bb5a8550, pnpm install, rustup + wasm-bindgen + Binaryen's wasm-opt as .github/actions/setup-rewriter-toolchain installs them, then ./cv npm --yes, which packs both tarballs). A local build will not match the sha256 pins byte for byte (build date, toolchain); after checking it says build bb5a855, update the pins here and say so in the notes

notes: scramjet: main at bb5a8550 (3.0.0-alpha, controller 0.0.15), the release tag "latest" as CI rebuilt it from that commit on 2026-11-23; the last stable release is v2.1.0 (controller 0.1.0, 2b2adc6e), 62 commits behind: the v3 interceptor rewrite (client.Intercept, WebIDL machinery), event interception, referrer, CSP meta, Trusted Types and incumbency work
service worker: the demo's sw.js at / (scope /) importing /controller/controller.sw.js; it only forwards requests to the controller (the file is the same at 517206bc, v2.1.0 and bb5a8550)
one Controller in the host page (as the demo and bootstrap): fetch handling, HTML/JS/CSS rewriting and the transport all run on the host page's main thread, not in the service worker

scramjet config: the Controller's default (scramjet defaultConfig, what bootstrap/create-proxy-app use); the demo instead passes defaultConfigDev, which turns on debug flags (captureErrors, debugTrampolines, debugSourceURL, cleanErrors off) and allowInvalidJs off; those are dev aids and would slow it

flags in effect: sourcemaps on, destructureRewrites on, encapsulateWorkers on, allowInvalidJs on, cleanErrors on, syncxhr off, incumbency "pst" where the engine hands out script hashes on CallSites (V8 does), else "lazystamp"; v3 has no allowFailedIntercepts flag (2.x had it, and the 2.x controller set it on before merging defaultConfig over it); read from the Controller in Chrome 159 on 2026-11-23: incumbency "pst"
no per-frame flag overrides (createFrame's new flags option); site flags live in the controller and none are set
URL codec: the controller default (encodeURIComponent under /~/sj/<controller>/<frame>/)
HttpCachePlugin on (demo and template both install it): caches upstream responses in the Cache API per RFC 9111, rewriting still runs on hits; no 304 revalidation

scramjet-utils 0.0.4 is packages/utils/src at bb5a8550 bundled with esbuild (npm has only 0.0.3, which pins 2.0.67-alpha.1 / 0.0.13 and lacks the v3 event interception); the demo's UrlWatcherPlugin and CatchEscapedLinksPlugin are UI plugins and are not installed

transport: epoxy (the demo offers epoxy and libcurl, default libcurl; epoxy chosen so every wisp contender uses epoxy); npm epoxy-transport 3.0.2 has stock epoxy-tls 2.1.20-1: the 16 KiB HTTP/2 header list limit STomp's patched build lifts, no HTTP/3, no ECH DoH
transport initializes lazily on the first proxied request (demo behaviour), so the epoxy wasm compile is inside the first load after boot
no cross-origin isolation headers on the host (the demo's vite server sends none)
